title: Hicham rachète l'agence ASK  (Hicham Buys the ASK Agency)

segments.t: We start in the agency lobby as Hicham arrives for his first morning. You'll hear the full scene in French first — just listen for the mood and voices.
Monsieur Janowski, vous êtes actionnaire majoritaire d'ASK avec soixante pour cent.
Toutes nos félicitations.
Merci beaucoup à tous.
Quand j'étais gamin, je rêvais d'être acteur.
Je voulais être une vraie star.
Vous vous occupez des acteurs, c'est votre domaine.
Je suis très heureux et enthousiaste d'être ici.
À votre santé!
Santé, monsieur Janowski.
Votre vrai nom, c'est Marteau?
Non, c'est juste un vieux surnom.
Ici, mon nom c'est Martel, d'accord?
Je ne veux pas gâcher notre lune de miel.
Santé, Andréa Martel!
Let's examine how Hicham introduces himself to his new partners.
Monsieur Janowski, vous êtes actionnaire majoritaire d'ASK avec soixante pour cent.

'Mr. Janowski, you are majority shareholder of ASK with sixty percent.' Mathias addresses his new boss using the formal 'you'. The term for someone who owns shares is built from a root meaning a share. A nice sentence in French.
Toutes nos félicitations.

'All our congratulations.' This polite phrase is built from a core meaning congratulations, joined by a plural possessive. You can say this whenever someone celebrates a major life event. A great expression in French.
Merci beaucoup à tous.
'Thank you very much to all.' Hicham greets everyone warmly. A handy chunk for addressing a group of people is literally 'to all'. You can say this in French.
Quand j'étais gamin, je rêvais d'être acteur.
'When I was a kid, I dreamed of being an actor.' Hicham shares a childhood memory. A common, everyday term meaning a kid or child is used here to set a casual tone. In French, this is widely used.
Je voulais être une vraie star.
'I wanted to be a real star.' Hicham admits his early ambition. The term for a famous celebrity is a clear cognate. The French love this expression.
Vous vous occupez des acteurs, c'est votre domaine.

'You take care of the actors, that is your field.' Hicham indicates his hands-off approach. The expression for an area of expertise comes from the concept of a domain or territory. In French, it fits perfectly.
Je suis très heureux et enthousiaste d'être ici.

'I am very happy and enthusiastic to be here.' Hicham expresses his excitement. A common term describes being happy, while the second is a recognizable cognate for feeling eager. A nice way to say it in French.
À votre santé!
'To your health!' Hicham raises a classic celebratory toast. This expression literally wishes good health upon the group, using the formal 'you'. In French, it is a great choice.
Santé, monsieur Janowski.
'Cheers, Mr. Janowski.' Andréa politely returns the toast. You can simply say the equivalent of 'health' as a shorter, casual way to clink glasses. The French find this natural.
Votre vrai nom, c'est Marteau?
'Your real name is Marteau?' Hicham teases his former classmate. He uses a common term meaning real or true right before the character's family name. In French, this sounds very fluent.
Non, c'est juste un vieux surnom.

'No, it is just an old nickname.' Andréa brushes off the embarrassing topic. The term for a nickname is built from a prefix meaning 'over' or 'extra' attached to a base meaning a name. The French use this structure often.
Ici, mon nom c'est Martel, d'accord?

'Here, my name is Martel, okay?' Andréa establishes her adult professional identity. A handy phrase for checking if someone understands or agrees translates literally as 'of accord'. In French, this phrasing is common.
Je ne veux pas gâcher notre lune de miel.

'I do not want to ruin our honeymoon.' Hicham playfully refers to their working relationship. The idiom for a honeymoon literally translates word-for-word as 'moon of honey'. You will find this useful in French.
Santé, Andréa Martel!

'Cheers, Andréa Martel!' Hicham seals the truce by addressing her with full respect. He pairs the casual toast with her first name and surname. This sounds extremely natural in French. Now let's listen to the celebration toast again at full speed.
Monsieur Janowski, vous êtes actionnaire majoritaire d'ASK avec soixante pour cent.
Toutes nos félicitations.
Merci beaucoup à tous.
Quand j'étais gamin, je rêvais d'être acteur.
Je voulais être une vraie star.
Vous vous occupez des acteurs, c'est votre domaine.
Je suis très heureux et enthousiaste d'être ici.
À votre santé!
Santé, monsieur Janowski.
Votre vrai nom, c'est Marteau?
Non, c'est juste un vieux surnom.
Ici, mon nom c'est Martel, d'accord?
Je ne veux pas gâcher notre lune de miel.
Santé, Andréa Martel!
Hicham Janowski is now the majority owner of ASK. While the toast is polite, his arrival brings an ambitious and unpredictable new dynamic to the team. See you next time!
À bientôt!
